title: Renewal
hookLine: temples rebuilt, texts reprinted, ordinations renewed

lines: ROW AFTER ROW OF WOODEN BLOCKS.
A SECOND TRY, BLOCK BY BLOCK.
WHAT PEOPLE DO AFTER A LOSS.
cards: On a mountain in Korea, at a temple called Haeinsa, long halls hold row after row of carved wooden blocks. Each block is a page of scripture, cut in reverse so it can be inked and printed.

The temple's story is that these blocks are a second try: an earlier set was lost to fire in a time of war, and monks and carvers sat down and made the whole thing again, block by block. Today isn't about a loss.
It's about what people do after one.

teach.b: Renewal comes in three kinds. Temples rebuilt: in Cambodia, Mongolia, China, and in exile in India, communities came back to ruined or empty halls and opened the doors again.

Texts reprinted: when a set of scriptures is lost, someone sits down and makes it again, like the carvers at Haeinsa. And ordinations renewed. You met the rule in Cambodia: a monk can't ordain himself.
Full ordination needs a gathering of monks fully ordained themselves, in a line that runs back, by tradition, to the Buddha. If that line dies out in a country, nobody there can give it.

Sri Lankan histories tell of a time when that happened, and of monks invited from Siam, today's Thailand, who came and gave ordination again. One branch of Sri Lanka's sangha still carries Siam's name.
Underneath sits a teaching the tradition never hid.

teach.h: DECAY IS INHERENT IN ALL COMPONENT THINGS.
teach.b: The Buddha's last words in the Mahaparinibbana Sutta, which this block first heard on the day about persecutions, are, in Rhys Davids's translation: "Behold now, brethren, I exhort you, saying, 'Decay is inherent in all component things! Work out your salvation with diligence!'" Decay is expected.
Temples, printing blocks and lines of teachers are all component things. Read this way, a loss isn't a sign that the teaching was false. It's the moment to work with diligence.
Carve again. Invite again. Open the doors again.

how: Buddhist communities rebuild damaged temples, reprint and recopy scriptures, and, where a line of ordination has lapsed, invite monastics from other countries to give ordination again.

games.q: you're a monk in a land where no fully ordained monks are left to give ordination. what do you do?
o: declare the line finished for good
invite monks from another land to give ordination again
hold an ordination anyway, without the monks it needs
games.why: Sri Lankan histories tell of monks invited from Siam who came and gave ordination again. one branch still carries Siam's name.

practice: Bring to mind something small that's broken or lapsed in your life, a habit you dropped, a friendship gone quiet, a chair with a loose leg, a practice that slipped, and look at it without scolding, the way the carvers looked at a blank block of wood.
Ask one question, what's the first small cut, and breathe with whatever answer comes.

wordCard.voice: Renewal. Temples rebuilt, texts carved again, ordination invited back: the tradition expects decay, and answers it with diligence. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali upasampada: full ordination as a monk or nun, given by a gathering of the fully ordained.

carryVoice: Your line: it renews. Decay is expected, and diligence is the answer to it. Until tomorrow.
